'''Andrew R. Barron''' is an American [[statistician]] and [[information theory|information theorist]]. He was the Charles C. and Dorothea S. Dilley Professor of [[Statistics]] and [[Data Science]] at [[Yale University]] until his retirement in 2024.<ref name="yale-dilley">{{cite web |title=Barron appointed Dilley Professor of Statistics and Data Science |url=https://news.yale.edu/2021/06/29/barron-appointed-dilley-professor-statistics-and-data-science |website=Yale News |date=June 29, 2021 |access-date=February 4, 2025}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Barron received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in Electrical Engineering and Mathematical Sciences from [[Rice University]] in 1981, and a [[Master of Science|M.S.]] (1982) and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] (1985) in Electrical Engineering from [[Stanford University]], where his doctoral advisor was [[Thomas M. Cover]].<ref name="conference-about">{{cite web |title=About the Workshop |url=https://yalefds.swoogo.com/infotheory/about |website=Yale Foundations of Data Science |access-date=February 4, 2025}}</ref>

After completing his doctorate, Barron joined the faculty at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], where he held appointments in the departments of Statistics and Electrical and Computer Engineering.<ref name="yale-dilley"/> In 1992, he moved to [[Yale University]],<ref name="yale-stats-history">{{cite web |title=The History of Yale University Department of Statistics 1963-2000 |url=http://www.stat.yale.edu/history/HistoryAmato.html |website=Yale Department of Statistics and Data Science |publisher=Yale University |access-date=February 7, 2025}}</ref> where he served as Chair of the Department of Statistics from 2001 to 2006.<ref name="yale-dilley"/>

== Personal life ==

Barron is a [[Fédération Aéronautique Internationale|FAI]] [[free flight (model aircraft)|free flight]] model glider competitor in the F1A class. He is a five-time U.S. National Champion, winning in 1984, 1987, 1992, 2007, and 2009.<ref name="nffs-nats">{{cite web |url=https://www.freeflight.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Nats-Winners-Glider.pdf |title=National Aeromodeling Championships Glider Winners |publisher=National Free Flight Society |access-date=February 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.org/details/nats-winners-glider |archive-date=February 7, 2025}}</ref>

* [[Claude E. Shannon Award]], [[IEEE Information Theory Society]] (2024)<ref name="shannon-award">{{cite web |title=Shannon Award for 2024 |url=https://www.itsoc.org/news/shannon-award-2024 |website=IEEE Information Theory Society |access-date=February 4, 2025}}</ref>
* Medallion Lecture, [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] (2005)<ref name="ims-medallion">{{cite web |url=https://imstat.org/archive-vol34-2005/ |title=IMS Bulletin, Volume 34, Issue 7 |publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |date=2005 |access-date=February 7, 2025}}</ref>
* Browder J. Thompson Memorial Prize, [[IEEE]] (1992)<ref name="ieee-browder">{{cite web |title=IEEE Browder J. Thompson Memorial Prize Paper Award |url=https://ethw.org/IEEE_Browder_J._Thompson_Memorial_Prize_Paper_Award |website=Engineering and Technology History Wiki |publisher=IEEE |access-date=February 7, 2025}}</ref>
* [[IEEE Fellow]]<ref name="yale-dilley"/>
